original_question: Which broad and mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds can be described explicitly? Here an affine Poisson manifold means a finite-dimensional manifold equipped with an affine atlas and a Poisson bi-vector P whose Schouten self-bracket [[P,P]] vanishes.
target_in_paper: The nearest official formulation available in arXiv:1910.05844 is the abstract-level open-problem theme concerning the integrability and analytic properties of Kontsevich graph-induced symmetry flows, specifically on known or “nearly generic” classes of Poisson brackets on finite-dimensional affine manifolds, rather than a general classification of affine Poisson manifolds themselves.
correct_elements: The draft correctly keeps the ambient objects finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds and the defining Poisson condition [[P,P]]=0 for the bivector P. It also correctly aims at an explicit-description question rather than a purely abstract cohomological one.
missing_details: The paper is not asking for a classification of affine Poisson manifolds as such; it asks about the action of known Kontsevich graph symmetries/flows on special classes of Poisson brackets.
The ambient manifolds are finite-dimensional affine real manifolds, i.e. smooth manifolds equipped with an affine atlas.
The relevant deformations are the universal infinitesimal graph-cocycle flows \dot{P}=Q(P) coming from Kontsevich’s oriented-graph construction, not arbitrary deformations of Poisson structures.
The intended meaning of “described explicitly” is: described explicitly enough to analyze the integrability and analytic behavior of the graph flow on that class.
The paper points to broad or “nearly generic” classes of Poisson brackets, not to all affine Poisson manifolds.
The draft omits the PDE/integrable-systems framing: the open problem is about studying these graph symmetries on such classes from that analytic viewpoint.
The draft omits that the question is about known symmetries of Poisson brackets, not about Poisson geometry in isolation.

Unlike some neighboring papers by the same authors, this target does not impose homogeneity, polynomial degree, or nilpotency restrictions; importing such restrictions would not be paper-faithful here.
refined_question: For which broad, mathematically natural classes of finite-dimensional affine real Poisson manifolds—that is, smooth manifolds with an affine atlas equipped with a bivector field P satisfying [[P,P]]=0—can the known Kontsevich graph-cocycle infinitesimal symmetries \dot{P}=Q(P) be described explicitly enough to study their integrability and analytic properties, i.e. to understand concretely how these universal graph flows act on such “nearly generic” classes of Poisson brackets?
justification: The draft is too broad because it turns the paper’s graph-flow problem into a general classification problem for affine Poisson manifolds. In the accessible text of arXiv:1910.05844, the paper itself states only at abstract level that its open problems concern the “integrability and analytic properties” of Kontsevich symmetry flows, “in particular, for known classes of Poisson brackets.” The contemporaneous conference abstract expanding the same note makes the target more precise: it is about the “action of known symmetries on classes of ‘nearly generic’ Poisson brackets,” which yields open problems from PDE and integrable-systems geometry. So the sharp stand-alone question should explicitly mention the Kontsevich graph-induced flows and the analytic/integrability goal, while retaining the affine-Poisson ambient setting. I did not add homogeneity or polynomial-degree assumptions because those belong to nearby later papers, not to this 2019 open-problems note.
